I am thinking about this year's planting. My 13.1 mu is split — I put wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as every year. Last year wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu and maize close to 550 kg per mu. That is okay but the neighbors with the new hybrid maize seed got better. I will try the improved seeds again this year.

For wheat, I use the compound fertilizer 15-15-15 at planting, about 50 kg per mu as base, then top-dress urea around 20-25 kg per mu at jointing. That gives me around 18 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K per mu. Wheat needs 3 irrigations from my well — winter water, jointing, and grain filling. I spray 2 times, once for aphids and once for rust if the weather is wet.

For maize, I plant after wheat harvest in June, no time to plough so I use rotary tillage. I apply about 40 kg compound as base and top-dress 25 kg urea at big trumpet stage — that comes to around 20 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Maize here needs 2 irrigations if rain is poor. I spray once for corn borer.

I will not change much from last year. Fertilizer prices are high, but cutting back is risky — better to spend the money than lose yield. My 2-person household, just me and my wife, we handle it ourselves except at harvest when I pay for the combine.
